title: Finite cohomological dimension on affine-diagonal schemes
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme over a field k with affine diagonal [def-weil-field] [def-pc-scheme]. There is an integer d_X >= 0 such that H^p(X,F)=0 for every quasi-coherent O_X-module F [pqf-def-coherent] and every p>d_X.

source.place: Tag 01XI, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines, finite cohomological dimension for quasi-coherent modules

proof.text: By Mathlib isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens choose a finite set s of affine opens covering the top open of X. Use I = s as the index type, with its Fintype structure and the linear order pulled back from Fintype.equivFin. The affine diagonal over Spec(k) makes pairwise intersections affine by isAffineHom_diagonal_iff applied to the top affine open of Spec(k). InfClosed.biInf_mem_of_nonempty then makes every nonempty finite intersection affine.

source.place: Tag 01XI, proof of coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines: finite affine covering and affine intersections

proof.text: Construct SiteCechComplex using the actual infima of the cover opens and inclusion maps. Their universal properties are the infimum universal property; all map identities follow because opens form a poset. Identify its full section complex with TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplex by identity degree maps: both differentials are the same signed face restrictions. Apply alternatingCechComputes. If p >= N = Fintype.card I, a strictly increasing Fin(p+1)-tuple would be injective and force p+1 <= N, a contradiction. Thus the ordered term is the trivial group, its degree-p homology is zero by ShortComplex.isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂, and the full Čech homology is zero by the comparison isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01XI, second proof of coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines: alternating Cech complex (Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-alternating-usual) vanishes in degrees >= t

proof.text: Apply Scheme.Modules.nonempty_cechComplex_linearEquiv_H using the affine nonempty intersections and the covering equality. Its inverse followed by cechComplexHomologyAddEquiv identifies ordinary H^p(X,F) with the zero abelian Čech homology group. Apply exists_moduleCohomology_source_comparison to identify module right-derived cohomology additively with ordinary H. The resulting injective map into a subsingleton makes the module cohomology a subsingleton, hence a zero ModuleCat object. Choose d=N, independently of F: d
